newsitem.title: USA: Butler U.S. business outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Butler U.S. business outlook positive.

text.p: Butler Manufacturing Co said Tuesday the outlook for its U.S. business is positive, despite a sharp fall in the company's earnings in the first quarter of 1997.

"As we approach the more active seasons for Butler's business, we sense a continuing strong level of demand in most all of the markets we serve," Butler chief executive Robert West said in a news release. "The outlook for our U.S. businesses is positive."
But Butler also said that recent foreign investments will continue to cause lower corporate earnings comparisons in the second quarter.
Those estimates are performing as expected, West said.
Total backlog for the building systems company of $271 million is 11 percent above the level of 1996, Butler said.

"Butler's construction services business had significantly lower first quarter sales and earnings than a year ago," West said. "They entered the year with reduced backlog, but recent success in procuring projects resulted in backlog at the end of the first quarter being 19 percent higher than a year ago."
Butler Tuesday reported net income of $1.9 million or $0.25 a share in the first quarter, compared to $3.3 million or $0.42 a share a year ago.
Start-up costs associated with the company's wholly-owned metal buildings subsidiary in China hurt first quarter earnings, Butler said.
